source.title: WRC Decisions with Frame by Frame Analysis
source.content:
Dear WCA Community,

With support from the WCA Board of Directors, the WCA Regulations Committee (WRC) has decided to retroactively apply the previously announced approach to [frame-by-frame analysis](https://forum.worldcubeassociation.org/t/wrc-statement-on-frame-by-frame-analysis/55294) to various past results. The process is documented in this [incident log](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/143).

For those unaware, the WRC’s previous approach was to only review footage at full speed when determining penalties, based on [this incident](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/50). However, it became readily apparent that the approach became inadequate for detecting violations that gave a significant advantage but were not visible at full speed. This most notably affected the 0.78 2x2 world record average.

To address this, the WRC changed its approach to reviewing footage frame-by-frame for certain results. Initially, this approach only applied to results set after the announcement was made – past results could not be reviewed using frame-by-frame analysis. This created a situation where past results were in violation of the WCA Regulations but could not be penalized, even if those violations resulted in a significant advantage.

Following further discussion, the WCA Board decided to return the decision on the 0.78 average to the WRC, as well as authorize the use of frame-by-frame analysis on past results to apply necessary penalties.
<!-- break -->
The WRC reviewed several past results that fell under the criteria listed in our approach to Frame-by-Frame analysis and voted on each of the attempts individually before coming to a final decision. Per the approach, only the timer starts could be penalized – timer stops were not to be analyzed with frame-by-frame analysis. Attempts were only penalized if the WRC determined with a strong degree of confidence that regulations were violated.

Much of the discussion surrounding this issue has been related to the 0.78 2x2 world record average. After analyzing these attempts frame by frame, the WRC determined that multiple attempts were in violation of the WCA Regulations. The results from our findings in reference to the 2x2 world record are summarized below. All +2 penalties are due to violations of [Regulation A4b](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A4b), and all +4 penalties are due to violations of both [Regulation A4b](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A4b) and [Regulation A4b1](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A4b1).


0.78 2x2 WR Average (Johor Cube Open 2024 Round 1)

* Attempt 1: 0.74 **(+4)**
* Attempt 2: 0.70 **(+2)**
* Attempt 3: 0.97 **(+2)**
* Attempt 5: 0.81 **(+4)**

0.90 2x2 WR2 Average (Dalian Open 2024 Round 1)

* Attempt 2: 0.49 **(+4)**


A public report on the analysis conducted on these attempts can be found [here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Hos7FEmNd_obKW2YOpUZEDHRhLOeTggi/view?usp=sharing). Information regarding other penalized results will not be released publicly out of respect for these competitors’ privacy. We request that the community not attempt to widely publicize the identity of those penalized and is respectful in discussions surrounding these incidents.

The rankings will be updated to reflect any changes shortly. Any appeals regarding the decision must be made by an affected party to the WCA Appeals Committee (WAC) at appeals@worldcubeassociation.org within 60 days of the announcement as per the [Disputes motion](https://documents.worldcubeassociation.org/documents/motions/16.2024.1%2520-%2520Disputes.pdf).

Community members are encouraged to forward any results fitting the criteria for frame-by-frame analysis privately to the WRC at regulations@worldcubeassociation.org if they believe that the Regulations were violated.

Once again, we would like to give you our deepest thanks to the community for your patience as we discussed and made this decision. Ensuring that the WCA Regulations are followed and maintaining the integrity of results at WCA competitions continue to be the WRC’s utmost priority. 

Signed,
The WCA Regulations Committee

translation.title: WRC 关于逐帧分析的裁决
translation.content:
各位 WCA 社区成员：

在 WCA 董事会的支持下，WCA 规则委员会（WRC）决定，将此前公布的[逐帧分析方法](https://forum.worldcubeassociation.org/t/wrc-statement-on-frame-by-frame-analysis/55294)追溯用于部分历史成绩。处理过程已记录在这篇[意外事件日志](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/143)中。

此前，WRC 根据[这起事件](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/50)所确立的做法，只以正常速度观看视频来判断是否应予处罚。但我们逐渐发现，这种方式无法识别某些虽带来明显优势、却在正常播放速度下看不出的违规。最受关注的例子便是二阶 0.78 秒平均世界纪录。

为解决这一问题，WRC 改变了做法，开始对特定成绩进行逐帧审查。最初，这一方法只适用于公告发布后创造的成绩，历史成绩不能通过逐帧分析重新审查。这就导致部分历史成绩虽然违反 WCA 竞赛规则，却无法受到处罚，即使违规行为带来了明显优势。

进一步讨论后，WCA 董事会决定将 0.78 秒平均成绩的裁决交回 WRC 处理，并授权对历史成绩采用逐帧分析，以作出必要的处罚。

WRC 审查了多项符合逐帧分析适用条件的历史成绩，并对每次还原分别投票，最终作出裁决。根据这一方法，只能对启动计时器时的违规作出处罚，不能通过逐帧分析审查停止计时器的动作。只有在 WRC 高度确信存在违规的情况下，才会对相应还原作出处罚。

围绕此事的讨论，很大一部分涉及二阶 0.78 秒平均世界纪录。逐帧分析这些还原后，WRC 认定其中多次还原违反了 WCA 竞赛规则。与二阶世界纪录相关的调查结果如下。所有加 2 秒处罚均因违反[规则 A4b](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A4b)，所有加 4 秒处罚均因同时违反[规则 A4b](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A4b)及[规则 A4b1](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A4b1)。

二阶 0.78 秒世界纪录平均（Johor Cube Open 2024 第一轮）

* 第 1 次：0.74 秒，**加 4 秒**。
* 第 2 次：0.70 秒，**加 2 秒**。
* 第 3 次：0.97 秒，**加 2 秒**。
* 第 5 次：0.81 秒，**加 4 秒**。

二阶 0.90 秒世界第二平均（Dalian Open 2024 第一轮）

* 第 2 次：0.49 秒，**加 4 秒**。

有关上述还原的公开分析报告可在[此处](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Hos7FEmNd_obKW2YOpUZEDHRhLOeTggi/view?usp=sharing)查看。为尊重相关选手的隐私，我们不会公开其他受到处罚的成绩信息。请社区成员不要试图大范围传播被处罚者的身份，在讨论这些事件时也请保持尊重。

排名将于近期更新，以反映上述调整。依照[争议处理动议](https://documents.worldcubeassociation.org/documents/motions/16.2024.1%2520-%2520Disputes.pdf)，受影响的当事方如需申诉，须在公告发布后 60 天内通过 appeals@worldcubeassociation.org 向 WCA 申诉委员会（WAC）提出。

如果社区成员认为某项成绩存在违规，且符合逐帧分析的适用条件，欢迎通过 regulations@worldcubeassociation.org 私下提交给 WRC。

再次衷心感谢社区在我们讨论并作出决定期间的耐心。确保 WCA 竞赛规则得到遵守、维护 WCA 比赛成绩的公正性，始终是 WRC 的首要任务。

WCA 规则委员会
